title: Everyday Figurative Idioms and Fixed Expressions

sections.content:
A **modismo** (idiom) pairs an everyday concrete image with a figurative meaning that you cannot deduce word for word: *meter la pata* literally says "put the paw in", yet it means "to put your foot in it" or make an awkward blunder.

In Spanish, the **noun and article inside an idiom are usually fixed**, while the **verb conjugates normally** for tense and person: *metí la pata*, *diste en el clavo*, *nos tomaron el pelo*. Pronouns that refer to the affected person appear as indirect objects (*me tomó el pelo* = he pulled my leg; *te echo una mano* = I will lend you a hand), and reflexive idioms keep their reflexive pronoun (*me quedé de piedra* = I was stunned).

Avoid swapping nouns or translating English idioms literally: you cannot say *dar en la uña* for "hit the nail on the head" (Spanish uses *el clavo*, an iron nail, not a fingernail) or *tirar de la pierna* for "pull someone's leg" (Spanish says *tomar el pelo*).

sections.title: High-frequency idioms and their figurative sense
rows: To blunder / put one's foot in it: *Metí la pata al mencionar la sorpresa.*
To hit the nail on the head: *Con ese comentario diste en el clavo.*
To pull someone's leg: *¿Me estás tomando el pelo o hablas en serio?*
To lend a hand: *¿Te echo una mano con las cajas?*
To be stunned: *Al oír la noticia nos quedamos de piedra.*
Not to mince words: *Ella no tiene pelos en la lengua y dice lo que piensa.*

items.spanish: Metí la pata al preguntar por un premio que todavía era secreto.
items.english: I put my foot in it by asking about a prize that was still a secret.

items.spanish: Con esa sola observación diste en el clavo y resolviste la duda.
items.english: With that single observation you hit the nail on the head and solved the doubt.

items.spanish: Al principio creí que me tomabas el pelo, pero luego vi la carta.
items.english: At first I thought you were pulling my leg, but then I saw the letter.

items.spanish: Cuando escuchó el anuncio final, todo el grupo se quedó de piedra.
items.english: When they heard the final announcement, the whole group was stunned.

sections.content: Keep the fixed noun and article intact (*la pata*, *el clavo*, *el pelo*, *una mano*, *de piedra*) and never translate English idioms word for word.
